title: Encrypted, Not Anonymous: A Hands-On Introduction to Confidential Solidity
description:
Confidential contracts stopped being theoretical faster than developer intuition adapted. OpenZeppelin Confidential Contracts is at v0.5.3, coprocessors are live on mainnet, and people are writing encrypted-state Solidity with plaintext habits.

We wrote and maintain the library, so this is a tour of our own mistakes, not just our features:

- Your contract stores values it cannot read. require() becomes a branchless select, and every guard you forget succeeds silently. 
- Arithmetic wraps instead of reverting. Since we can’t revert on encrypted conditions, our safe-math layer returns encrypted success booleans.
- Disclosure is irreversible. FHE access grants can't be withdrawn, and secrets can’t be forgotten.

Attendees complete a confidential contract, then break it themselves.

Before the session, install Foundry, clone github.com/arr00/devcon8-confidential-solidity-workshop, and run make ready (the README has the details).
abstract: Building for confidentiality adds a dimension of complexity to the Solidity we've written for a decade: your contract stores values it cannot read, failures don't revert, and arithmetic wraps silently. We'll build with OpenZeppelin Confidential Contracts, then break what we built, so you can spot the failure modes that only exist when state is encrypted.
